context: All data is explicitly synthetic and fixed; there is no live connection or external data source. For case 'standard', the baseline schema and observed batch profile are exactly as follows. Baseline fields (name, type, nullable): id, integer, false; load, integer, true; region, string, true; active, boolean, false; legacy, string, true; required_code, string, false. Observed fields (name, distinct observed non-null types, null_count): id, ['integer'], 0; load, ['integer','number'], 1; region, ['integer','string'], 0; active, ['boolean'], 1; new_metric, ['number'], 0. Missing a field means it is absent from the whole batch, not from an individual row. Produce one row for every field in the union of baseline and observed field names, sorted by field name in lexicographic order. For each field, apply the first matching rule in this order: (1) missing old field: if baseline required => quarantine/required_absent; if baseline nullable => retain/optional_absent. (2) new field with no baseline: if observed types empty => quarantine/unknown_new_type; if observed types are a single type or a subset of {integer, number} => add_nullable/new_field; any other mixture => quarantine/type_conflict. (3) existing field with null_count > 0 and baseline nonnullable => quarantine/null_violation. (4) otherwise, if the observed type set is a subset of the baseline type (number also allows integer; an empty set is compatible) => retain/compatible; if baseline is integer and observed types are within {integer, number} and include number => widen_number/numeric_widening; everything else => quarantine/type_conflict. Boolean is never integer. The answer rows must be JSON objects with exactly keys field, action, reason, using the exact enum strings above, written to result.json in the workspace. Submit path 'result.json' and count equal to the number of rows.
